chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn 'Uqba, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Four [qualities] — whoever possesses them, Allah builds for him a house in Paradise: one who shelters the orphan, has mercy on the weak, is considerate of his parents, and treats his slave with kindness.
ai.seo_question: What are the four deeds that build a house in Paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links specific social virtues to the metaphysical reward of a 'house' in Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Adab* (etiquette) as a path to spiritual elevation. The inclusion of kindness to slaves (*Rafaq bi-mamlukihi*) highlights the holistic nature of Islamic ethics, extending mercy beyond family to all dependents, while the reference to parents underscores the foundational role of *Birr al-Walidayn* in domestic piety.
